doc.title: Harold Danko interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 28, 2021

title: Joining Woody Herman and the Satin Doll initiation
summary: Compared with school, his first Woody Herman gig, got through Joe LaBarbera, tested him on a Satin Doll intro.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Well I’m going to leapfrog a bit. If you think about what you learned in those classes, in that environment, compared to what you might have learned on the Woody Herman band, can you compare and contrast that?

Well I mean I’m really glad that I had that preparation and when I got with Woody’s band, which was my first real, I would say, real professional gig you know, with some kind of people noticing it and you had to be on your toes, I at least had the background to do the reading, and I knew enough tunes. There was a little initiation test that Woody had, because there were some charts that were fake, the rhythm section — so my first gig, you know all the cynical guys on the — I had just gotten out of the Army so I was just the happiest guy with my short hair, to be on Woody Herman’s band. And some of the guys would say, oh we were playing like an Elks Club or something, my first gig, one of those things. And the guys were saying, “Every night’s a jazz festival” you know. So we go to this Elks Club, and people had said, “Don’t bother to say hello to Woody” or

whatever, “just do the gig” and whatever. And so Joe LaBarbera, who had gotten me on the gig, said oh by the way, some of the charts, like there’s no rhythm charts on like “Satin Doll” and “A Train.” He said, “Do you know those Duke Ellington intros on those?” And I said, “Yeah, pretty much I could do it on ‘Satin Doll’” or whatever. He said, “Good, because Woody will just count it off and that’s what you do for the intro.” And not knowing it’s like really the initiation test, the first tune with Woody Herman he just like walked on and kind of had a look at me, ah there’s a new piano player, number 300 or whatever. And he says, “Satin Doll intro, one, two” and I went [scats] and it’s like I looked at Joe LaBarbara and it was like okay, you’ll be on the gig I think, you know.
So I guess if you just played a 1-6-2-5 or whatever, 1-4-3-6 even, it wouldn’t have made it.
I see. That’s so fascinating that, how musicians get plugged into those bands, like there’s no rehearsal, it’s like you’re thrown into the fire and you hope you survive I guess.
And the guy who recommended you’s ass is on the line. So Joe LaBarbara’s ass —
